newsitem.title: GERMANY: Weather benefits German grain, oilseeds - Toepfer.
newsitem.headline: Weather benefits German grain, oilseeds - Toepfer.

text.p: Plantings of German winter grain and oilseeds for harvesting in 1997 had been completed under favourable conditions, grain trader Toepfer's latest monthly market report said on Friday.
Weather patterns had benefited grain and rapeseed already in the soil and crops were looking in good shape, it said.
Overly dry weather in September made way to above average precipitation in October, it noted.
Toepfer reiterated farm ministry estimates earlier this month that grain plantings had risen by an overall four percent to 5.35 million hectares.
Winter wheat and barley sowings were up four percent each at 2.65 million and 1.48 million ha respectively.
Rye was seen down four percent at 780,000 ha and triticale up around 25 percent at 450,000 ha.
